BreakEvenAnalysis.Context: Allison suggested running break-even scenarios after hearing Westbrook might raise rent. Based on 2025 actuals.

CurrentState.Note: Aaron's draw is informal - not a fixed obligation. Raj's $1200 is contractual.

Scenario_A_RentTo850.Label: Rent increases to $850/mo (Westbrook hint)
Scenario_A_RentTo850.BreakEvenCalculation: Fixed costs $2,915 + $150 increase = $3,065. At $95/member, need $3,065 / $95 = 32.3 → 33 members minimum (assuming no other revenue). With drop-ins + equipment, effective break-even ~30 members.
Scenario_A_RentTo850.Impact: Net income drops $150/mo. Still very healthy at 60 members. Concern is psychological - sets precedent for future increases.

Scenario_B_RentTo1000.Label: Worst case - rent to $1,000/mo
Scenario_B_RentTo1000.Impact: Manageable. Would need to reassess if combined with other cost increases.

Scenario_C_MembershipDropPlus RentIncrea.Label: Rent to $850 AND membership drops to 50 students
Scenario_C_MembershipDropPlus RentIncrea.Impact: Still profitable but Aaron's draw becomes tight. Would need 33 members just to cover costs. Below 40 members = red flag for sustainability.

BreakEvenAnalysis.KeyInsight: Break-even is ~33 members at current cost structure, ~34 with $850 rent. Current 60 members provides 82% buffer above break-even. Real risk isn't the rent increase alone - it's rent increase + seasonal membership dip (historically Dec-Feb lowest at ~55 members).
